reason: Machine lens: all opcodes are real on the 65SC12. LDX zp (A6, 3 cycles, 2 bytes) replaces LDA zp, and STX abs (8E, 4 cycles, 3 bytes) replaces STA abs (back &56, crtc_start_address_high/low &B0/&B1, flip_* &2A48-&2A4A in the listing), so those cost the same. TRB abs (1C, 6 cycles, 3 bytes) is in the 65SC02 set the 65SC12 has; only the Rockwell bit ops are missing. Baron already assembles TRB (zp form in the listing) in these cmos = TRUE sections. Old cost: JSR 6 + SEI 2 + LDA &FE34 4 + AND# 2 + STA 4 + CLI 2 + RTS 6 = 26; new: 6; a saving of 20 cycles. Bytes are 3 for 3, so nothing after &9373 moves and no branch or indexed read changes page. A = &04 at player_done: it comes from LDA #&04 at &935D, and the two stores after it leave A alone; nothing else branches to player_done. Clearing bit 2 through TRB matches AND #&FB. The 65C02's RMW does an extra read of ACCCON, which has no side effects, and an IRQ cannot split one instruction. No self-modifying operands or code-as-data in &9364-&9378. cpu_sees_main stays, because cpu_sees_back branches to it. The I = 0 assumption belongs to the semantics lens; the candidate's own measurement (19.98 a pass) agrees with the count.
